title: So.Sta. — Social Statistics
text:
Social Statistics Research Group


So.Sta. brings together statisticians, social statisticians and sociologists working on complex social and health data. We develop and apply quantitative methods to study population health, ageing, inequalities, welfare, environmental determinants and the translation of evidence into policy.


So.Sta. stands for Social Statistics. In Italian, sosta also means a pause: a reminder to stop, look closely at the data, and think before acting.


Meet the teamExplore our projects

title: So.Sta. — Social Statistics
text:
What we work on



Methods


Complex data & inference


Models and inferential tools for dependent, hierarchical, high-dimensional and heterogeneous data, with an emphasis on valid and interpretable inference.




Applications


Population health & inequalities


Ageing, morbidity and multimorbidity, health surveillance, territorial and socioeconomic inequalities, and environmental determinants of health.




Impact


Evidence into action


Communication tools, accessible statistical outputs and interdisciplinary work designed to support public-health stakeholders and policy decisions.










Current project


PLANET4HEALTH


So.Sta. members contribute to the Horizon Europe project connecting environmental and climate science, public health and social science to support evidence-based planetary-health policy.


Read more →







Our home


Based at Ca’ Foscari University of Venice


So.Sta. is primarily rooted at Ca’ Foscari, while keeping an open collaborative network across institutions and disciplines.


  Università Ca’ Foscari Venezia

title: Projects
text:
Active · 2024–2027



Translating Science into Policy: A Multisectoral Approach to Adaptation and Mitigation of Adverse Effects of Vector-Borne Diseases, Environmental Pollution and Climate Change on Planetary Health.


PLANET4HEALTH is a Horizon Europe project developing knowledge, data and tools on how environmental degradation affects human, animal and ecosystem health. The project connects environmental and climate science, public health, epidemiology and social sciences, with a strong focus on translating evidence into policy.


Project website




Past · 2023–2025



Ageing Well in an Ageing Society.


Age-It is a national extended partnership on ageing that brings together demographic, biomedical, technological, economic and social perspectives. Its goal is to support an inclusive society for all ages and to make Italy a leading research hub on ageing.


Project website

title: Projects
text:
Themes connecting our projects



Healthy ageing


Morbidity compression, multimorbidity, life-course trajectories and social inequalities in ageing.
